                    ### Question
                    Immunology researchers attempt to characterize the role of several cytokines in a 5-year-old male’s allergic reaction to peanuts. Months after initial exposure to peanuts, the child was brought to the ER due to repeat exposure with symptoms of anaphylaxis that resolved following epinephrine injection and supportive therapy. Which of the following best describes the role of IL-4 in the child’s response:?

                    ### Options
                    opa. B cell class switching
opb. Stimulates IgA production
opc. Macrophage and Th1 cell activation
opd. Neutrophil chemotaxis
ope. Growth of cytotoxic T cells

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
IL-4 is primarily involved in B cell class switching and Th2 cell differentiation, leading to the production of IgA. This aligns with the consensus that IL-4 plays a key role in promoting antibody class switching to IgE and IgG1 in allergic responses.
